window-1.title: cozyweb — a Sublime collection
window-1.blurb: It's a whole shelf of hand-made, gatekeeper-free corners of the internet collected by an actual person, and I guarantee you'll come out the other side wanting to build your own weird little site.

window-2.title: 2026 is the Year of the Zine — Commonplace Zines
window-2.blurb: A tiny independent newsletter making the case that folded, stapled, gloriously imperfect paper is having its moment again — which feels like an engraved invitation for you to start a zine as your next side quest.

window-3.title: Cucumber Basil & Citrus Mocktail
window-3.blurb: You make your own basil syrup and pack the glass with hand-cut cucumber matchsticks — it's less a drink than a tiny green installation, and exactly the kind of fussy-on-purpose hosting move you'd commit to fully.

window-4.title: Yellowtrace — Home Tours
window-4.blurb: It's a properly indie design journal full of warm, object-crammed homes — vintage lamps, hand-thrown pottery, colour used with nerve — and its Asia-Pacific eye means you'll actually see rooms that feel like they could exist near you.

window-5.title: Mad Roaster's Slow Bar, Enabling Village
window-5.blurb: A slow bar buried inside Enabling Village, run by a team that hires refugees and pours coffee like it's a ritual — exactly the kind of place you'd sit in for three hours, sketch something, and end up befriending the barista.
